content.comment_body: Hello, I am using a [product_name] controller ([version_no]) that runs continuously with 24/7 power, and I want to continuously log both input and output data. While testing, I observed correct data until there was a power failure. After the power outage, the controller produced odd data values. I had attached an Excel file showing the data returned by the PLC. There is no initialization button in the circuit, since the controller is designed to run immediately once power resumes. Thank you in advance.
The circuit diagram is attached as requested.
It turned out that the problem was a bug related to the [product_name] ([version_no]). [company_name] should address and resolve this issue. I have been waiting for a solution for a long time.
Hi, Have you received any solution yet? I am experiencing the same problem—data logging becomes inconsistent after a power failure. Thank you.

Any error correction from [company_name] would require new firmware. Since updating firmware on this model is not possible, it would mean purchasing new hardware. Additionally, [company_name] does not provide any change log with new firmware releases. How would you know if the issue is fixed? Just buy the new hardware and hope for the best?
Could you clarify what you mean by '[company_name] published no change log with a new firmware'?

[company_name] currently does not disclose if firmware errors are corrected in their products or when a new firmware version is released. You may want to consult with your sales contact at [company_name] about this.

analysis.insight_summary: Users have noted that following a power outage, the data logging feature in the [product_name] controller ([version_no]) produces incorrect and unreliable values, undermining data integrity. The situation is further aggravated by the inability to update firmware easily, which means addressing this issue requires replacing hardware. There is also dissatisfaction with [company_name]'s lack of clarity about firmware bug fixes.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect dependable and consistent data logging, even after power interruptions. They also want clear information about firmware updates and bug resolutions, preferably without having to replace their hardware.
pain_keywords: incorrect log values after power failure
